beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Paul was handing on something sacred that he had received himself: on the very night he was betrayed, at supper with his friends, the Master took a simple loaf of bread into his hands and gave thanks over it.

timing.text: Paul was handing on something sacred that he had received himself: on the very night he was betrayed, at supper with his friends, the Master took a simple loaf of bread into his hands and gave thanks over it.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

timing.text: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then he lifted the cup. This one, he said, was the sign of a new covenant — a solemn promise sealed between God and his people, and offered freely to them.

timing.text: This one, he said, was the sign of a new covenant — a solemn promise sealed between God and his people, and offered freely to them.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

timing.text: After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ever since, his people have taken that same bread and that same cup together, quietly, reverently — a small, holy act of remembering the One who gave everything for them.

timing.text: Ever since, his people have taken that same bread and that same cup together, quietly, reverently — a small, holy act of remembering the One who gave everything for them.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord's death till he come.

timing.text: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord's death till he come.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And it looks in two directions at once. Every time we take it, we are remembering a sacrifice already made, and we are looking forward, in hope, to the day he returns.

timing.text: And it looks in two directions at once.
Every time we take it, we are remembering a sacrifice already made, and we are looking forward, in hope, to the day he returns.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.

timing.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Paul asked for just one thing beforehand, and he asked it gently: that each person pause and look honestly into his own heart, and come sincerely. Not to keep anyone away, but so the moment stays real and tender.

timing.text: Paul asked for just one thing beforehand, and he asked it gently: that each person pause and look honestly into his own heart, and come sincerely.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Here is the quiet study gem. This is why it is done again and again, and never just once. It is a covenant renewed — week after week, a fresh chance to be made clean, to set down the past and begin again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And a place at that table is kept for you. Not for the perfect, but for the sincere — for anyone willing to come and remember. When the bread and the cup are offered to you, will you come to the table?
